correctness.summary: The exact centered-fiber identity reduces the obstruction to maxima of Binomial(n,p) fiber degrees. One-mode fibers are independent; all-mode upper bounds require only a fixed-factor union bound. Chernoff plus a one-mass Stirling lower bound gives the sharp large-deviation exponent, while a Poisson-relative binomial mass asymptotic and tail-ratio sum give the second-order lattice profile. The sublogarithmic formula follows from the same rate comparison. Deterministic exact-tail calculations support the formulas.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Zhou and Zhu (2026) prove the log-free tensor-norm upper bound, note the fiber obstruction, and give only a fixed-fiber logarithmic lower bound plus qualitative sublogarithmic divergence; their maximum-degree lemma uses a nonsharp Chernoff constant. Classical Poisson-like triangular-array and random-graph extreme-value theory is prior art and the scalar maximum law is not claimed. The claim is restricted to the tensor-specific sharp fiber constant, second-order localization, polynomial-tail obstruction, necessary C >= sqrt(h^{-1}((k-1+r)/c)) dependence, and quantitative sublogarithmic refinement. The full Anderson-Coles-Husler (1997) text was not directly inspected, leaving residual risk for the scalar component.

value.summary: The result resolves the unavoidable constant contribution hidden behind the source theorem's order-optimal sqrt(d) statement, quantifies the dependence on tensor order, sparsity, and requested polynomial tail, and gives an explicit second-order and sublogarithmic fiber profile useful for sharpening sparse tensor concentration.

limitations: The exact second-order center is stated for d=c log n.
The exact lattice limit is for one fixed mode; the all-mode maximum is only localized within O_P(1).
The result is a lower obstruction and does not determine the full injective-norm limiting constant.
Classical discrete-extreme theory may subsume the scalar maximum calculation.
The full Anderson-Coles-Husler (1997) article was not directly inspected.
Independent audit has not been performed.
